status: Read-only investigation and proposed test-helper design; no source edits, no repaired runtime pass.
authorization: Lead requested independent read-only fdinfo/readlink investigation while third Android device diagnostic source inputs were frozen.

observed_device_kernel.boundary: Public commit resolves the Git abbreviation embedded in the device uname; this is not an independent binary-to-source/reproducible-build attestation.

observed_denial.meaning: Successful duplicate ownership does not grant getattr permission for every inherited descriptor. Third positive control failed; no source/lifetime pass from this observation.

conclusions: fdinfo seq_show resolves an FD under the table lock and holds a struct file reference while emitting the header: pos, flags, mnt_id, ino. ino is file_inode(file)->i_ino, independent of path spelling and directory-entry deletion.
fdinfo does not call vfs_getattr for its header, but proc/LSM/ptrace read permissions still apply. Actual same-app read access to every relevant own fdinfo entry has not been executed by this review.

vfs_getattr invokes security_inode_getattr; even fstat of an owned duplicate can therefore encounter the observed pmsg_device denial. Using a different ordinary allowed metadata interface does not disable SELinux or grant new permissions.
Generic stat copies inode->i_ino, but filesystems may override getattr. Do not universally equate fdinfo ino and st_ino without validating the controlled regular-file/pipe fixture assumptions.

Raw mnt_id+ino equality is not a safe cross-process identity filter: cloned/bind mount objects can have different allocated IDs for the same underlying superblock/inode. A transferred provider FD can reference a mount absent from the consumer mount namespace. Mapping only the consumer mountinfo cannot prove a negative in that situation.

Stable dup readlink is useful for diagnostic categories, but /dev/pmsg0 is an absolute character-device path rather than a socket/anon_inode marker. A growing path exclusion list or exact basename matching cannot establish general regular-file/pipe identity and risks missed hardlink/deleted-path aliases.

For this controlled fixture only, strict fdinfo inode-prefilter plus same-inode fstat confirmation is a conservative approach: unrelated different-inode FDs require no getattr; every same-inode collision still needs successful native device/inode comparison and can fail rather than falsely return zero.
proposed_invariants: Keep production sources, source/destination assertions and the real denied Os.link case unchanged. This is a test measurement correction only.

Keep target native st_dev/st_ino and cross-process pipe Bundle semantics. Verify each known target is REG or FIFO and its actual owned descriptor has fdinfo ino equal to fstat st_ino. A mismatch or unsupported field fails the measurement; it cannot authorize a zero result.

Validate the actual provider-owned normal-file descriptor and actual reliable-pipe descriptor before IPC transfer as well as caller-owned positive controls. Close provider-owned resources on any validation failure; never adopt/reflect into the production RawSource FD.

Snapshot numeric own FD names before probing. Duplicate each original, never adopt or close it. Only initial duplication EBADF from a concurrently closed original can be ignored, as in the held implementation.

Read only the fixed, bounded fdinfo header of the stable probe-owned duplicate. Require an unambiguous numeric ino; if mnt_id is parsed retain it as diagnostic metadata, not a negative identity filter. Missing, malformed, duplicate, overflow or inaccessible data must fail closed, not return null/zero.

If validated header ino differs from the target, do not call fstat. If equal, fstat and compare actual dev/ino. A same-inode protected FD/collision or any other fstat error still fails; no EACCES catch-and-continue.
Close both the header reader and every probe-owned duplicate on every path. Never read/write/seek the original open file description; metadata inspection must leave offsets unchanged.

A descriptor scan is not an atomic global census. Positive controls and measured target operations must keep their known handles stable while asserting counts; source acquisition/close races and arbitrary concurrent descriptor churn are not newly certified.
Do not log raw fdinfo, mountinfo, inode tables, descriptor numbers or backing paths. Retain only bounded aggregate diagnostics or fixed OS-node categories when explaining a concrete denial.
required_controls_before_claiming_pass: Execute inside the same actual instrumentation app/SELinux domain, not only adb shell, run-as, host Linux or Robolectric.

Deliberately hold two descriptors for one regular fixture (including a genuine dup), observe 2 then1 then0 across real closes, repeat scans and require unchanged offset. The zero-descriptor assertion must reject the intentionally open file.

Use two independently opened regular files and require the target count unaffected by the other. Confirm an actual FileProvider-returned descriptor agrees with the local fixture inode calibration across IPC.
Create a real pipe, verify both ends fdinfo/fstat match FIFO identity, assert2 then1 then0 and no duplicate leak. Keep actual provider reliable-pipe error tests as integration checks.

Capture a regular target identity, unlink its owned name while keeping its handle open, still detect one handle, then detect zero after close. Do not normalize away deleted suffixes or require a surviving name.

Retain actual symlink/canonical alias tests and the real hardlink test. The existing Os.link EACCES remains a failed/unavailable hardlink-acquisition scenario unless a separately reviewed legitimate fixture can exercise it without changing device policy.

Test strict parser missing/duplicate/nondecimal/negative/overflow/overlong inputs as parser-policy evidence, not fabricated native inode evidence. Distinguish a valid unrelated inode zero from missing identity, and never accept target inode zero.

Prove no catch converts inaccessible fdinfo or same-inode fstat errors into empty success. Known injected reader failures may exercise this policy separately but do not replace the actual protected-FD diagnostic.

Inspect actual rerun XML, source hashes and target counts including the positive controls. Previously failed complete test methods remain failures; passing preceding assertions is not passing the method.
remaining: No repaired helper source or runtime execution exists at this review checkpoint. Actual fdinfo app-domain permission and target calibration require the lead-authorized next diagnostic window.
